heading: BLOOM helps communities do this themselves.
intro: The people who know a community best are already there. BLOOM partners with locally rooted organizations, which we call Civic Hosts, that can bring people together across difference. We give them the infrastructure to turn that trust into consequential public action.

items.label: Funding
items.title: Funding
items.desc: We help level the playing field by providing resources for engagement, research, communications, facilitation, and the work required to bring a whole community into the process.
items.alt: Residents filling a community forum in Cache County, Utah

items.label: Training + methods
items.title: Training + methods
items.desc: Running a good public process is a craft. Hosts receive training, tested methods, playbooks, coaching, peer learning, and access to researchers and practitioners.
items.alt: A facilitator organizing ideas on a wall of sticky notes at the Utah Solutions Forum

items.label: CivicOS
items.title: CivicOS
items.desc: Our open-source civic infrastructure helps communities combine in-person and digital participation, engage hundreds or thousands of people, and see clearly where people agree, where they differ, and what matters most.
items.alt: Delegates working at tables with laptops at the Utah Solutions Forum

networkLine: And a national network: no community should have to solve the AI transition alone.
